title: Introduce pin resolution modes + semver-range support with performance-profile awareness
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Customers pin models in multiple ways today (tag, semver-like tags, commit hash). We do not have a first-class strategy for semver ranges (e.g. ^1.4, ~2.0), nor a clear runtime behavior when a pinned selector resolves to multiple compatible artifacts with different published performance profiles. This causes two classes of problems: 1) unexpected runtime upgrades when label formats change, 2) hidden performance regressions when a selector resolves to a variant with different latency/cost characteristics.

Goal: Add a consistent, opt-in 'pin resolution mode' and semver-range support in the API and SDKs that: (a) permits semver range selectors, (b) gives callers choice of strictness (strict/compatible/lenient), (c) factors published performance profiles into selection and provides deterministic fallback rules, and (d) preserves backward compatibility for existing simple tag/hash pins.
acceptance_criteria: API accepts semver-range selectors (caret ^, tilde ~, exact) in model pin fields and rejects invalid range syntax with clear error codes.
New optional query parameter/field 'pin_mode' supported: 'strict', 'compatible', 'lenient'. Default behavior remains current resolution for existing clients.
When pin_mode=strict: only exact semver matches or exact tag/hash accepted; ranges are rejected with a 400 unless a single exact match exists.

When pin_mode=compatible: resolve semver ranges to the highest release that satisfies the range and whose published performance profile meets or exceeds the requested 'profile' threshold; if none, follow documented fallback order.
When pin_mode=lenient: resolve to highest matching release ignoring profile differences but emit a warning telemetry event and response header with resolved version metadata.
SDKs (JS, Python, Go) expose pin_mode and semver-range helpers and surface resolution warnings as an opt-in SDK callback/event.
Runtime emits structured telemetry for every resolution: requested selector, resolved identifier, profile mismatch flag, decision path, and source (catalog/alias/hash).
Docs and migration guide published and linked from error messages for invalid pins or profile mismatches.
Backward compatibility: calls that omit pin_mode continue to behave as today (no surprise rejection), and existing tag/hash pins remain fully supported.
E2E tests covering a matrix of selectors (exact tag, semver ^, semver ~, hash) x pin_mode x profile thresholds pass in CI.
Rollout plan validated on canary routing for 2 weeks without customer regressions before org-wide availability.
proposal:
High level approach:
1) Catalog extension: allow model metadata to include semver-style 'release' annotations and a machine-readable performance_profile slug (e.g. 'low_latency', 'balanced', 'high_throughput') plus numeric metrics (p50_ms, tokens/sec, memory_gb).
2) API: add optional fields to the inference request: 'pin_selector' (string), 'pin_mode' (string enum), and 'profile_hint' (string). Backward-compatible default: pin_selector continues to accept tag/hash as today; pin_mode absent means legacy behavior.
3) Semver parsing: reuse a tiny semver library on control plane to evaluate ranges; accept caret ^ and tilde ~ ranges and exact semver. Reject complex range expressions (||, >=< combinations) in v1 to keep behavior deterministic.
4) Resolution logic in control plane: create a deterministic comparator that ranks candidates by: exactness (exact match > range match), release recency (highest semver), performance_profile match (equal/above requested profile), and stable alias preference. The comparator changes slightly depending on pin_mode (strict enforces exactness; compatible enforces profile threshold; lenient relaxes profile check).
5) Runtime: resolved model id and metadata are attached to the request context and propagated to serving plane. If profile mismatch occurs and pin_mode!=lenient, runtime should attempt documented fallback (try lower minor within range or fallback to configured default model) and surface clear error/warning.
6) SDKs: expose helper builders that validate semver syntax locally and can pre-warn before hitting the API; allow an onResolution callback for visibility.
7) Telemetry & logs: structured events with decision path. Add new metrics for 'profile_mismatch_count' and 'resolution_mode_usage'.
api_examples: Example 3 - strict rejects range: { "model_pin": "redwood-llama-3@^1.4.0", "pin_mode": "strict" } -> 400 Bad Request (if no exact match present)
Response header: X-Resolved-Model: redwood-llama-3@1.4.2; X-Resolved-Profile: low_latency; X-Pin-Mode: compatible
sdk_changes: JS/Python/Go: add optional parameters to client.request({ model_pin, pin_mode, profile_hint })
Add local semver_range.isValid() and .satisfies() helpers in SDKs to surface early validation errors
Expose onResolution(resolutionMetadata) callback that receives resolvedId, resolvedProfile, matchedSelector, and warning flags
Default behavior: SDKs do not enable 'strict' by default to preserve existing customer behavior
Version bump notes: call out new fields in CHANGELOG and add migration snippets
rollout_plan: 1) Implementation behind feature flag in control plane and SDKs. 2) Enable semver parsing and pin_mode in internal test org and Redwood demo tenants. 3) Canary: route 5% of traffic for 2 weeks to new resolver with telemetry and 'auto-fallback' disabled (fail-open only when safe). 4) After 2 weeks and no critical regressions, enable auto-fallback for pin_mode=compatible. 5) Gradually increase to 100% and document opt-out for orgs needing strict legacy behavior.
migration_notes: For customers who used tags that implicitly behaved like ranges, provide a short migration doc: 1) Search for requests using tag-like patterns in audit logs. 2) If you depend on implicit range semantics, add pin_mode=compatible and a profile_hint. 3) For strict reproducibility, pin to exact hash or semver exact release (e.g. @1.4.2). 4) Notify customers via in-console banner and link to the migration playbook.
tests: Unit: semver parser edge cases (^, ~, exact, invalid strings)
Unit: comparator behavior across candidate lists with different profiles
Integration: control-plane resolution returns expected resolved id and headers for each pin_mode
E2E: SDK pre-validation + server-side resolution + serving-plane model used (compare token-level latency against published profile)
Chaos: simulate catalog alias flip where alias points to a newer release and ensure compatible mode respects profile threshold
